title: Mach Number: Not a Speed, But a Ratio
h1: Mach number — the speed unit that changes with the weather
description: Mach 1 at sea level is 340 m/s. Mach 1 at 40,000 ft is 295 m/s. Here is why a Mach number is not a constant speed and how to convert it.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: Mach is not a unit — it is a ratio to the local speed of sound. And the local speed of sound depends on temperature, which depends on altitude.
body: Fighter pilots quote Mach. Air-traffic controllers quote knots. Physicists quote metres per second. Only the last is a real speed. Mach and knots both hide dependencies that change with the atmosphere.

> Speed of sound in dry air: a = 20.05 × √T(K) m/s
> Sea level, 15°C: 340.3 m/s = 1,225 km/h = 661.5 kn
> 30,000 ft, −44°C: 303 m/s = 1,090 km/h = 589 kn
> Mach = TAS / a (both in same units)

Temperature drops about 2°C per 1,000 ft up to the tropopause (~36,000 ft), then stays roughly constant. The speed of sound tracks √T. A Concorde cruising at Mach 2.02 at 55,000 ft was doing 605 m/s (~2,180 km/h). Descending to sea level at the same Mach 2.02 would mean 687 m/s (~2,475 km/h) — physically the same 'Mach number' but 82 m/s faster in true airspeed.

Aircraft pitot tubes measure dynamic pressure, converted to indicated airspeed (IAS). Density decreases with altitude, so IAS underreads TAS at altitude. A 787 cruising at Mach 0.85 at 40,000 ft has IAS around 290 kn but TAS around 490 kn. Ground-speed shown on the seatback screen includes wind.

At 40,000 ft, ISA temperature is 216.7 K, so a = 295.1 m/s. Mach 0.85 × 295.1 = 250.9 m/s = 903 km/h = 487 knots TAS. Compare to sea-level Mach 0.85: 289 m/s = 1,041 km/h = 562 kn. Same Mach, different speeds.
Mach = ratio, not a speed. Sound speed = 20.05 × √T(K). At cruise altitude, Mach 0.85 is about 900 km/h TAS. At sea level, it is about 1,040 km/h.

faqs.q: Why is Mach 1 slower at altitude?
faqs.a: Cold air. Speed of sound depends only on temperature (not pressure or density in an ideal gas). Altitude → colder → slower sound.
Orbital velocity from low Earth orbit, roughly. Space Shuttle reentry began around Mach 25 at 122 km altitude.

faqs.q: Do supersonic booms depend on Mach?
faqs.a: Yes — the shock cone half-angle μ = arcsin(1/Mach). Higher Mach = narrower cone = louder boom over a smaller ground track.
